Smoothing parameters with raised end values

Source: R/diagnostics.R
hp_schedule.Rd

hp_schedule() gives the smoothing parameter of every observation (or second difference) under the end-point schemes of Hanif, Iqbal and Choudhary (2017, eqs. 9a and 9b): \(\lambda\) in the middle and \(\lambda + \alpha j^{i}\) for the \(j\)-th of the \(k\) values at each end, counted from the middle (\(j = k\) at the first and last observation).

Usage

hp_schedule(T, lambda, alpha, k, power = 1, form = c("rows", "differences"))

Arguments

T

length of the series.

lambda

the base smoothing parameter.

alpha

the weight \(\alpha \ge 0\).

k

number of raised values at each end.

power

\(i\): 1 (linear, default) or 2 (quadratic); any positive number is accepted.

form

"rows" (default: \(T\) values, one per observation, as in the published code) or "differences" (\(T - 2\) values, one per second difference).

Value

A numeric vector of smoothing parameters.

See also

fmhp_filter, hp_loss

Author

Muhammad Yaseen (myaseen208@gmail.com)

Examples

hp_schedule(
    T      = 50
  , lambda = 100
  , alpha  = 10
  , k      = 20
  , power  = 1
  , form   = "rows"
  )
#>  [1] 300 290 280 270 260 250 240 230 220 210 200 190 180 170 160 150 140 130 120
#> [20] 110 100 100 100 100 100 100 100 100 100 100 110 120 130 140 150 160 170 180
#> [39] 190 200 210 220 230 240 250 260 270 280 290 300
